First patient dosed in phase 1/2 study evaluating SOBI003 for treatment of mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA)

Swedish Orphan Biovitrum AB (publ) (Sobi™) announces that the first patient has been dosed in the phase 1/2 study SOBI003-001. The study is an open-label, non-controlled, multiple-dose study with the objective of assessing the safety, tolerability and efficacy of SOBI003 in nine children aged 1-6 years for the treatment of mucopolysaccharidosis type IIIA (MPS IIIA), also known as Sanfilippo A syndrome.

“Since there is currently no treatment available for MPS IIIA, the initiation of this study is an important first step towards finding a potential treatment for this debilitating disease,” says Milan Zdravkovic, Chief Medical Officer and Head of Research & Development at Sobi.

“I am very pleased that we were able to enrol the first patient in this important study. We look forward to learning more about how SOBI003 may potentially be able to help patients in the future as we enrol more patients into the study,” says Dr. --------------------------------------------------------------------------------

### 2.3. SOBI003 Administration

The study drug was administered as a weekly infusion over a period of 4 h via a central venous access port. A single dose of a non-sedative antihistamine was administered within 30 to 120 min prior to each infusion. The infusion duration could be prolonged to up to 24 h if infusion-related reactions (IRRs) occurred, at the investigator's discretion. In case of identified IRRs, the investigator could decide to administer symptomatic treatment, such as antipyretics (for example, acetaminophen), corticosteroids or additional antihistamines.

The starting dose of SOBI003 for the first three patients enrolled in the FIH study, Cohort 1, was 3 mg/kg. During the extension study, the individual dose of SOBI003 was adjusted, as proposed by the SRC, and at the discretion of the investigator. Patients who started at 3 mg/kg could have their dose escalated to 10 mg/kg and subsequently to 20 mg/kg during the extension study; likewise, patients starting on 10 mg/kg could receive 20 mg/kg. An overview of the individual patient dose levels is shown in Fig. 3.

10 Augusti, 2018 09:00

Swedish Orphan Biovitrum AB (publ) (Sobi™) meddelar att den första patienten har doserats i fas 1/2-studien SOBI003-001. Det är en öppen, icke-kontrollerad, multipeldos-studie av nio barn i åldern 1–6 år med mukopolysackaridos typ IIIA (MPS IIIA), även kallad Sanfilippos syndrom A. ”Jag är mycket nöjd att vi har inkluderat den första patienten i denna viktiga studie. ## Abstract

Purpose: Mucopolysaccharidosis IIIA (MPS IIIA) is an inherited lysosomal storage disorder caused by mutations in the N-sulfoglucosamine sulfohydrolase gene that result in deficient enzymatic degradation of heparan sulfate (HS), resulting in progressive neurodegeneration in early childhood and premature death. A chemically modified variant of recombinant human sulfamidase, SOBI003, has shown to cross the blood-brain barrier (BBB) in mice and achieve pharmacologically relevant levels in cerebrospinal fluid (CSF). We report on a phase 1/2, open-label, first-in-human (FIH) study (NCT03423186) and its extension study (NCT03811028) to evaluate the long-term safety, tolerability, pharmacokinetics/pharmacodynamics (PK/PD) and clinical efficacy of SOBI003 in patients with MPS IIIA for up to 104 weeks.

# First Sanfilippo Syndrome Type A Patient Receives Sobi’s Investigational SOBI003

Written by Patricia Inácio, PhD | Aug. 14, 2018

Image: SOBI003

  *   *   *   * Swedish Orphan Biovitrum AB’s (Sobi) has dosed the first patient in its Phase 1/2 clinical trial evaluating SOBI003 to treat Sanfilippo syndrome type A.

The SOBI003-001 study (NCT03423186), which is still recruiting participants, intends to assess the therapy’s safety, tolerability and effectiveness when delivered to Sanfilippo A children, 1 to 6 years old, who have not received prior treatment.

Nine children will be enrolled from two clinical sites in the U.S. — the Childrens’s Hospital and Research Center, Oakland, California (recruitment active) and the University of North Carolina Hospitals — and from Gazi University Hospital, Turkey.

Participants will be divided into three groups, each receiving escalating doses of SOBI003, starting at 3 mg/kg and delivered directly into the blood (intravenously), once a week for 24 weeks.

The product candidate SOBI003 has been developed in-house by Sobi and is a chemically modified variant of recombinant human sulfamidase, using Sobi's proprietary glycan modification technology Modifa™.
